# entire-api — agent notes

Per-jurisdiction Go service: HTTP API + two NATS workers (repo-activity,
user-activity) over two Postgres stores (`repo`, `usr` schemas). See
[README.md](./README.md) for architecture and [CONTRIBUTING.md](./CONTRIBUTING.md)
for build/test.

## Conventions an agent must not get wrong

- **Database migrations use a UTC-timestamp version, never a hand-picked
  integer.** Create them with `scripts/new-migration.sh <repo|user> <name>` →
  `internal/store/migrations/<store>/YYYYMMDDHHMMSS_<name>.sql`. goose tracks by
  the filename's version number and silently skips any version `≤` the current
  DB version, so two PRs picking the same next integer (e.g. both `016_…`) make
  one migration vanish with no error. Leave the existing `001…0NN` files as-is.
  Full rationale: [CONTRIBUTING.md](./CONTRIBUTING.md#database-migrations).
- **Never renumber or edit a migration that has been merged _and applied_** —
  add a new (timestamped) one. Merged alone is not the test. A migration can sit
  on `main` having never reached a database, which is exactly what happens when
  `migration-check` blocks the deploy that would have applied it. Ask
  `refs/deploy/staging` — the last commit whose migrations reached a database:
  `git fetch origin refs/deploy/staging` and see whether the file is in that
  tree. In it, leave it alone; absent from it, restamping it forward is the fix,
  and usually the only one (the deploy stays blocked until the version moves).
  To settle it from a database instead, ask the catalog, not
  `information_schema` (which hides tables the reading role has no grant on) and
  not `goose_activity_repo` (`operator_ro` has no grant on it):
  `SELECT to_regclass('repo.<table the migration creates>');`
- **A `trailforge.NewServiceForge` reason must be registered in entiredb's Core
  before it works, and registering it takes two edits there.** The reason string
  is a cross-repo contract with no enforcement on either side: Core admits an
  exact `(workload, reason)` pair, and nothing here fails when it doesn't. In
  `entiredb`'s `core/api/sts_token.go` you need **both** a row in
  `githubInstallationTokenCapabilities` *and* the reason added to that
  authority's arm of `validFor` — a row without the `validFor` entry is still
  rejected. Grep entiredb for the reason string in the same change that
  introduces it here.

  This fails silently by design: every service-forge caller is best-effort, so a
  denied mint is logged and swallowed and the feature simply never acts. Two
  shipped dead this way (`runner_checks_failed`, `trail_gate_checks_resync`). One
  was worse than a no-op — `gaterecompute` treats a failed check-run read as
  fail-closed, so the denied mint flipped the checks gate to a **blocking
  `error`**, meaning the resync route broke the gate it exists to repair. If a
  forge-backed feature does nothing in prod and nothing is in the logs, check
  the reason is admitted before reading any further.
- **Run `mise run build`, `mise run vet`, `mise run lint` before pushing.**
  Integration tests (`mise run test:integration`) need Docker and self-skip
  without `ACTIVITY_TEST_DATABASE_URL`; plain `mise run test` stays unit-only.

## Testing cross-cell behaviour

`internal/multicellular` is the cross-jurisdiction suite — several real cells
(embedded NATS + real Postgres each) driven over real transport; the only CI suite
that's cross-cell, real-transport, and real-store at once. See its README for the DSL.

# brainstore

Region-local hosted store for Entire Brain durable facts ("memories").
Each fact is one row keyed `(repo_id, fact_id)` — the fact id is a content
hash, so identity is stable across branches and machines — plus immutable
provenance anchor rows (session, checkpoint, commit, turn). Clients push
facts through an idempotent batch upsert and pull a repo-wide change feed,
filtering locally by git reachability. Brainstore sits behind the
entire-api gateway and stores everything in the region's Aurora Postgres —
a repo's facts never leave its home region.

Branch names are display metadata, never storage keys: renames, deletions,
and recycled branch names cannot strand or misroute memories (COR-2110 v3
design; built as COR-2123).

## How it works

- **Per-fact rows are the source of truth.** An upsert verifies every
  record's content-derived id (`sha256(normalized text + sorted paths)`);
  one forged record rejects the whole batch. New ids insert with
  server-stamped attribution; existing ids union anchors and advance
  status one way (`active → superseded|retracted`, `superseded →
  retracted`) — regressions are ignored, so re-uploads are no-ops.
- **The feed re-delivers on change.** `updated_at` (server-stamped) is the
  feed keyset and bumps only on material change (new anchor, status
  advance, kind fill, trail stamp), so retractions and merges flow to
  every puller without churning on idempotent re-uploads.
- **Trails attach by anchors.** When core reports a trail merged (with its
  session/checkpoint/commit membership), matching facts get a `trail_id`
  stamp; facts uploaded later — e.g. a session that ends after a squash

input.description:
From a customer ticket: a repo hosted natively on Entire ran `entire brain publish` and got "hosted publish currently supports github.com-hosted repos only".

## Investigation result: publish has NO deployed server for ANY host

The original plan (make the server's brain-artifacts slug resolver handle native repos) is moot:

- `POST /repos/{repo_id}/brain/artifacts` exists in **no deployed service**. entire-api main has zero brain files and zero brain routes (verified by fresh clone, grep, and `git log -S`). brainstore (et/entirehq/brainstore — the real hosted memories server) serves only facts upsert, the change feed, the memories read model, and trail-merged stamping; it has never had an artifacts endpoint.
- The live prod API spec (us cell) has no `/brain/artifacts` route.
- Recorded Brain facts confirm: the hosted brain-bundle server exists only in **unmerged** entire-api PRs #744–#752 (+#242), ~1,800 commits and 97 migrations behind main with red CI; and MemDEKStore was rejected for hosted brain storage — a durable DEK store is a prerequisite for enabling hosted publishing at all.
- So `entire brain publish` fails for github.com repos too (the request would 404); Entire-native users merely hit the client-side host gate first.

Meanwhile the actual user need — manually pushing memories — is already served: `entire brain memories sync` is hosted-only over the per-fact wire, addresses the server by the connect binding's repo ULID, and works on Entire-native repos today (the customer's sync succeeded).

## Decision needed (product)

1. **Retire or hide `entire brain publish`** until a bundle server exists, pointing users at `memories sync`; or
2. **Revive the server stack**: brain-artifacts endpoint (entire-api or brainstore), durable DEK store, and host-aware repo identity so native (`et/`) repos render canonical wire keys — at which point the client should take the wire `repo_key` from the server-resolved placement, not the origin remote.

Recommendation: (1) for the memories use case; (2) only if hosted bundle retrieval is still on the roadmap.

## Shipped now (safe under either outcome)

entire-brain: every publish wire-repo_key refusal (non-github host, unresolvable remote) now names the supported path — `memories sync` on a connected repo works for any host. This removes the customer's dead end without prejudging the server decision.
